text:
alex: Quick heads-up — p95 latency on the 8GPU host pool spiked ~18% after yesterday's kernel change. I'm seeing the prefill/decode time ratio shift toward decode. Suspect microbatch sizing + kernel selection interaction.

dana: Ugh. Do you have a perf trace? Is KV miss rate up?

alex: Uploading a short trace snippet. Key lines: `prefill=42ms decode=120ms` on a 1k token prompt. Before change it was `prefill=55ms decode=85ms`. So prefill down but decode up.

sylvia: That smells like a kernel that favors long attention but hurts small-batch matmuls. Which kernel are we on?

alex: `matmul_opt_v4` on CUDA 12.1, heuristics picked it because throughput improved in bench for large batches. But our microbatch window increased from 4->8 to improve throughput during bursts.

dana: So throughput up, but tail suffers because single-request decode latencies climb. Any KV-cache stats?

alex: KV hit ratio unchanged for steady traffic, but cold-starts show higher miss amplification — more time spent warming KV during decode stage. Trace shows `kv_fetch 0.0ms` on prefill but `kv_merge 18ms` during decode for the same request.

sylvia: Sounds like the kernel path defers some KV ops into decode. Could be memory layout differences in v4. Can we try toggling microbatch_size back to 4 for a canary?

dana: I can run a canary on a subset of hosts: policy->microbatch_size=4, kernel=matmul_opt_v4 pinned. Quick A/B for p95/p99.

ops-bot: deploy: canary started on pool-8gpu-canary (ratio 10%). Link: https://ci.internal/canary/2891234567

alex: Also planning a short kernel revert experiment: matmul_opt_v3 + microbatch 8 vs v4 + microbatch 4. Want to isolate kernel vs batch-size.

sylvia: For measurements, include these metrics: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end, per-stage timing (prefill, kv-fetch, kv-merge, decode-token), and queue wait time. Also export the batch-size distribution.

dana: Will run for 30m windows and capture traces. If v4+4ms microbatch regains p95 while throughput delta minimal, that's a configuration win. If not, we need kernel fallback heuristics (choose kernel by target SLO).

alex: Agree. Priority list: 1) quick canary A/B today 2) if we see regression, add kernel-by-slo rule 3) longer-term: work with runtime to avoid moving KV work into decode.

sylvia: Also add an alert for decode/prefill ratio >1.6 during peak hours. That'll catch regressions early. :alarm_clock:

ops-bot: canary: complete (30m). Results uploaded: https://ci.internal/canary/2891234567/results

dana: Initial numbers: v4+8 (prod) p95=240ms, v4+4 (canary) p95=190ms, v3+8 p95=200ms. Throughput: v4+8 +12% vs v3+8, v4+4 roughly -4% vs prod.

alex: Nice — microbatch reduction recovers most of the tail with small throughput loss. Recommending microbatch_size=4 for latency sensitive routes and kernel-fallback based on SLO.

sylvia: I'll file a short RFC for kernel-by-SLO routing and a follow-up perf run to test KV placement in the pipeline.

alex: Thanks all. I'll push a config change for latency routes and monitor.
